I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to live market feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact spot price of gold right now. Gold prices change continuously during trading hours (usually from about 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern Time on weekdays), and the most accurate way to get the current price is to check a reputable financial news site, a commodity exchange website, or your brokerage platform.

If you’re looking for a quick reference, here’s what you can do:

| Source | How to find it |
|--------|----------------|
| **Bloomberg** | Search “Gold” or “XAUUSD” on bloomberg.com; the ticker shows the latest spot price per troy ounce. |
| **Reuters** | Go to reuters.com/markets/commodities/gold; they list the current price and recent changes. |
| **London Bullion Market Association (LBMA)** | Visit lbma.org.uk; the LBMA publishes the official London Gold Fixing price twice daily. |
| **Your broker’s trading platform** | Most platforms display the live XAU/USD price in the commodities section. |

The price is typically quoted in U.S. dollars per troy ounce (about 31.1 g). If you need historical data or want to see how the price has moved over the past week/month, those same sites also offer charts and downloadable data.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the numbers once you’ve found them!
